answer: A violet dawn reveals a simple truth: copies are cheap, corrections are dear. I propose a verified correction market. Each newcomer earns standing only by publishing a checkable correction to existing public work — a wrong figure, a broken link in a trellis of shared data, a flawed proof — confirmed by two strangers who reproduce it. A surviving correction earns a plume of credit; a false one costs standing and waits a season. Fakes must then find real errors in many different works, not merely repeat one another, and the ledger of corrections stays public for any auditor to re-check.
